newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, Dec 20 - For the second consecutive month PORLA's figures on CPO production/palm oil stocks revealed no surprises as they came close to our estimate. CPO production fell 13.8 percent or 122,300 tonnes to 762,500 tonnes in November. Both Peninsular Malaysia and East Malaysia posted identicle declines of 13.8 percent. Compared to November last year, production grew a modest 2.6 percent. For the 11 months to November, production expanded 8.2 percent or 589,300 tonnes to 7.748 million tonnes.

East Malaysia enjoyed a strong growth of 16 percent with its production amounting to 1.803 million tonnes or 23.3 percent of the country's output. The continuing wet weather throughout the country had delayed harvesting operations in most producing areas, particularly in Kuantan and Terengganu. Tentatively we estimate production in December to drop around 15 percent to 650,000 tonnes. This would bring production for the whole of this year to around 8.4 million tonnes, and increase of 7.5 percent or 590,000 tonnes over 1995. Palm oil disappearance fell to 761,400 tonnes in November from a fear of 824,500 tonnes in October.

PORLA's prelimary palm oil exports in November showed a big drop of 96,000 tonnes to 632,400 tonnes from the recorded level of 728,400 tonnes registered in October. The November exports fell short of our estimate of 655,000 tonnes. With CPO production matching disappearance in November, stocks of palm oil remained little changed at 956,000 tonnes as against 954,800 tonnes (revised) at end October. The figure is in line with our estimate of 960,000 tonnes. Stocks of CPO alone rose marginally to 604,800 tonnes from 602,700 tonnes a month earlier.

As expected, CPO stocks shrank in East Malaysia but show an increase of 7,300 tonnes to 454,000 tonnes in Peninsular Malaysia. With CPO production continuing its seasonal downtrend but palm oil disappearance expecting to be maintained, stocks of palm oil are tentatively estimated to drop some 95,000 tonnes to around 860,000 tonnes at end December or unchanged from the year ago level. The firmness in the palm oil market this week reflected expectations for a drop in stocks to below the 900,000 tonnes level. CPO futures rose 33-24 ringgit with March posting the week's high of 1,247 ringgit before settling at 1,238 ringgit yesterday.

The market is now at its highest level in 15 weeks. February/March RBD olein was quoted at $565, up from $560 last Friday while RBD stearin rose to $400 from $392.50. RBD palm oil also posted a similar increase of $7.50 to $530.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
